allow.2.2a: b⁻ⁿ has one value for each base and exponent. Every power a student works out by hand is drawn: squares to 25² and of tens to 100², cubes to 10³ and 20³, the small 4th, 5th and 6th powers, and 2⁷ to 2¹⁰. That is 57, less the test's 4⁻² and 5⁻². More would test long multiplication, not exponents.
allow.2.2b: (−c)⁻ᵉ has one value for each base and exponent: the same hand-worked powers as 2.2a, odd and even, less the test's (−3)⁻³.
allow.2.2c: (1/d)⁻ⁿ has one value for each base and exponent: the same hand-worked powers as 2.2a, less the test's (1/2)⁻³.
allow.2.3: The value of b⁻ⁿ again, as a choice, with n to 4: the same hand-worked powers as 2.2a.
allow.3.2a: v⁻ⁿ = 1/vⁿ has one number, the exponent (2 to 9). A new letter is not a new version, and a longer exponent would only lengthen the ladder picture.
